title: Machine-learning-assisted target prioritization and experimental validation of the neoeriocitrin-mTOR axis in impaired osteogenic differentiation.
authors: Wang, Yuhao; Luo, Jianguang
abstract: Neoeriocitrin (NEO) is a citrus-derived flavonoid with potential osteoprotective activity, but its pharmacological targets and mechanisms in impaired osteogenic differentiation remain unclear. Osteoporosis-related differentially expressed genes were intersected with predicted NEO targets, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, random forest, and support vector machine analyses consistently prioritized MTOR for mechanistic investigation. Molecular docking predicted a favorable binding pose of NEO at the 12-kDa FK506-binding protein (FKBP12)-mTOR FKBP12-rapamycin-binding (FRB) interface, while the cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) demonstrated increased cellular thermal stability of mTOR following NEO treatment, supporting an mTOR-associated intracellular effect. In dexamethasone-treated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, NEO dose-dependently restored alkaline phosphatase activity, mineralized nodule formation, and the expression of runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2), osteopontin (OPN), and alkaline phosphatase (ALP). NEO also enhanced autophagic flux, increased the microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B)-II/LC3B-I ratio, reduced p62 expression, and suppressed dexamethasone-induced phosphorylation of mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) and ribosomal protein S6 kinase 1 (S6K1). Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy with 3-methyladenine (3-MA) and mTOR overexpression both attenuated the pro-osteogenic effects of NEO. Collectively, these findings support an mTORC1-associated S6K1 signaling mechanism linking NEO treatment to autophagy regulation and osteogenic differentiation. NEO may therefore represent a candidate natural compound for further preclinical investigation in osteoporosis-related bone loss.

title: Scoparone attenuates ethanol-induced hepatocellular injury through PI3K/Akt-mediated regulation of oxidative stress and apoptosis.
authors: Wei, Min; Qi, Weiwei; Fang, Yu; Chen, Zhen; Gao, Ya
journal: The Journal of pharmacy and pharmacology
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Scoparone (SCO) has demonstrated hepatoprotective potential in previous studies, whereas its molecular mechanisms against alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) remain unclear. This study investigated the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of SCO in ethanol-induced HepG2 cells. METHODS: Network pharmacology and molecular docking were employed to predict the potential targets and signaling pathways of SCO against ALD. Ethanol-induced HepG2 cells were used to validate the predicted mechanisms by biochemical assays, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence staining, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction and western blotting. KEY FINDINGS: Network pharmacology identified 109 overlapping targets between SCO and ALD, with the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) signaling pathway emerging as a key pathway. SCO enhanced alcohol metabolism, attenuated oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and suppressed ethanol-induced apoptosis. Mechanistically, SCO activated PI3K/Akt signaling, thereby enhancing nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2/heme oxygenase-1 (Nrf2/HO-1) antioxidant signaling and suppressing the phosphorylated forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)/FoxO1-associated apoptotic signaling. These protective effects were markedly reversed by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. CONCLUSIONS: SCO protects against ethanol-induced hepatocyte injury by activating the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, thereby enhancing Nrf2/HO-1-mediated antioxidant defense and suppressing FoxO1-associated apoptotic signaling. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic evidence supporting further preclinical investigation of SCO in alcohol-associated liver injury.

title: Isoliquiritigenin Modulates Quorum Sensing-Associated Neutrophil Extracellular Trap Formation in COPD Isolate Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
authors: Dhanyashree, Honagodu Ravichandra; Charavu, Rakshitha; Hameed, Asif; Karthika, Kizhakkumkara; Mynalli, Adarsh Basavaraj; Surya, Suprith; Bhandary, Yashodhar Prabhakar; Shastry, Rajesh Padumane
abstract: We characterize a virulent COPD isolate, P. aeruginosa RS85, as a potential inducer of NET, and demonstrate the ameliorating impacts of isoliquiritigenin (ISL) on bacterial quorum sensing (QS) and neutrophil responses. Low doses of ISL exhibited anti-quorum sensing (AQS) activities on P. aeruginosa RS85 and PAO1, while its high dose was found to be bactericidal. Significantly high amounts of ROS and NETosis were observed in neutrophils when treated with the live cells and secretome of clinical P. aeruginosa, whereas P. aeruginosa PAO1-JP2 elicited markedly reduced responses. RS85 secretome promoted pulmonary NET formation, recruitment of inflammatory cells, alveolar destruction, and emphysema-like pathology in mouse lungs in vivo. The introduction of ISL inhibited cell- and secretome-mediated ROS and NETosis to the levels observed in PAO1-JP2. ISL treatment constrained NETosis, the co-localization of myeloperoxidase and citrullinated histone H3, lung inflammatory damage and structural damage in vivo. The molecular docking of ISL with bacterial QS (LasR and RhlR) and neutrophil NADPH oxidase assembly (p47phox and NOX2) proteins showed strong ligand binding, substantiating interference in QS signaling and ROS generation pathways. This study identifies potential QS-regulated secretory virulence in clinical P. aeruginosa driving NETosis, and demonstrates the ISL-mediated amelioration of NETs and bacterial QS.

title: Atractylenolide II Alleviates 5-Fluorouracil-Induced Intestinal Toxicity Through Potentially Targeting the TLR4-Mediated MYD88/NF-kappaB Signaling Pathway: An Integrated In Silico and In Vitro Study.
authors: Liu, Yangzhi; Jia, Ru; Liu, Yue; Liu, Pengpeng; Xu, Huiying; Liu, Yue; Chen, Yuxin; Huan, Jingyu; Yu, Haoran; Qu, Yang; Cai, Qian
abstract: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a potent compound in anti-tumor chemotherapy; however, its clinical utility is hampered by dose-limiting intestinal toxicity. Atractylenolide II (AT-II), a bioactive sesquiterpene derived from Atractylodis Rhizoma, has reported anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective activities. In this study, we employed an integrated strategy combining chemical characterization, computational pharmacology, and in vitro experiments to investigate the protective effect of AT-II against 5-FU-induced intestinal toxicity and clarify its potential target-associated mechanism. UHPLC-QE-MS was applied to profile the constituents of Atractylodis Rhizoma, with AT-II subjected to subsequent computational and experimental analyses. ADMET evaluation, network pharmacology, molecular docking, 100 ns molecular dynamic (MD) simulation and DFT calculation were performed to predict druggability, candidate targets and molecular interaction features. TLR4 and HIF1A were screened as hub candidates. MD simulations revealed that the AT-II-TLR4 complex exhibited much better conformational stability than AT-II-HIF1A. DFT calculations suggested that the lactone moiety of AT-II exhibits pronounced electron-rich features. The DARTS assay provided evidence for a potential interaction between AT-II and TLR4. In IEC-6 cells, 20 muM AT-II rescued 5-FU-impaired cell viability, decreased the release of pro-inflammatory IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha, and suppressed the TLR4/MYD88/NF-kappaB inflammatory cascade by inhibiting NF-kappaB p65 phosphorylation. Taken together, these results suggest that AT-II protects against 5-FU-induced intestinal toxicity, probably via modulation of TLR4 and downstream MYD88/NF-kappaB inflammatory signaling, offering preliminary in vitro evidence for developing AT-II to ameliorate chemotherapy-associated intestinal toxicity.

title: MicroRNA Gatekeepers: Integrating Growth, Development, and Stress Adaptation in Cotton.
authors: Li, Jiarui; Wang, Xuan; Qin, Jiawang; Wu, Yifan; Wei, Mengyao; Li, Chaofan; Jia, Yanfeng
abstract: As the primary cash crop for natural fiber, cotton develops under sophisticated endogenous genetic programs, with biotic and abiotic stresses continuously driving its adaptive evolution. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional regulators that modulate gene expression via target mRNA cleavage, translational repression, and mediation of DNA methylation. miRNAs target transcription factors and hormone signaling pathways to regulate cotton plant architecture and fiber development. In addition, miRNAs mitigate biotic and abiotic stresses through ROS, lignin, and hormone pathways, as well as by forming competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) modules with long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs). This review establishes an miRNA-centered regulatory framework that coordinates cotton growth, development, and stress resistance. A series of technologies, including multi-omics combined with machine learning, gene overexpression, STTM, MIM, MIGS, CRISPR editing, foliar dsRNA spraying, and bionanocarriers, are proposed to facilitate the breeding of cotton varieties with high yield, superior fiber quality, and broad-spectrum stress tolerance.

title: Activity of Fluoro-Substituted 3,5-Di[(E)-Benzylidene]piperidin-4-Ones with N-Arylsulfonyl Appendages Against KRAS-Mutant Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Cells.
authors: Ghosh, Hindole; Azaz, Duha Qamar; Saxena, Addhyan; Bodenhausen, Nicole; Schobert, Rainer; Biersack, Bernhard; Dandawate, Prasad
abstract: KRAS-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a high mortality that still lacks efficient therapies. Monoketone-based bisarylidene curcuminoid derivatives have shown promising activities against various PDAC models. Based on our previous findings on anticancer-active N-acryloyl-modified piperidin-4-one derivatives, we replaced the reactive acryloyl moiety by a series of N-arylsulfonyl bis-difluoro/trifluoromethylbenzylidene piperidin-4-one derivatives and tested them for antiproliferative activity against KRAS-mutant PDAC cells. Furthermore, apoptosis induction based on caspase-3/7 activation and STAT3 inhibition were investigated for the most promising compound. Notably, the N-tosyl derivative 3a with 4-trifluoromethyl substituents at the benzylidene rings exhibited the highest antiproliferative activities against PDAC cells (IC(50) = 0.22-0.26 microM, 48 h). Derivative 3a also strongly induced apoptosis in PDAC cells and suppressed STAT3 activation/phosphorylation, which was supported by molecular docking of this curcuminoid into the SH2 domain of STAT3 and by 3a-STAT3 binding confirmed using CETSA in MiaPaCa-2 cells. These findings identify compound 3a as a promising lead for further preclinical evaluation in KRAS-mutant PDAC models and in other STAT3-dependent cancer types.

title: Inositol-Dependent Alleviation of Lithium-Induced Embryonic Neurotoxicity in Mice Through the GSK3beta/beta-Catenin/CyclinD1 Pathway.
authors: Li, Shen; Guo, Jin; Wang, Xiuwei; Guan, Zhen; Zhu, Zhiqiang; Yang, Aiyun; Wang, Jianhua
abstract: Lithium carbonate (Li(2)CO(3)) is a first-line pharmacotherapy for bipolar disorder (BPD) in female patients of childbearing age, although it is associated with embryonic teratogenicity. Lithium exposure in batteries and pharmaceuticals has been a toxicity factor for women's reproductive health in energy, environment, and fitness fields. Neural tube defects (NTDs) are the severest reproductive outcome of maternal Li(2)CO(3) exposure. Currently, there is a lack of effective prevention for Li(2)CO(3) neurotoxicity. Our previous study revealed that lithium-induced murine NTDs correlated with enhanced proliferation and impaired inositol biosynthesis. In this study, 400 mg/kg inositol was used to treat the lithium-induced murine NTDs after calculating the toxicity using ADMETlab 3.0 and Deep-PK. We found that inositol supplementation ameliorated fetal neural phenotypes, crown-rump length, and body weight and rescued aberrant cell proliferation and dysregulated the GSK3beta/beta-catenin/CyclinD1 pathway in both animal and cellular models. The affinity of GSK3beta-inositol interaction was analyzed and validated using molecular dynamics and surface plasmon resonance. GSK3beta-edited cell models further revealed that inositol altered GSK3beta post-transcriptional status and phosphorylation, consequently modulating the GSK3beta/beta-catenin/CyclinD1 signaling cascade. Overall, our study clarified that inositol alleviates lithium-induced NTDs via the GSK3beta/beta-catenin/CyclinD1 pathway, revealed the direct molecular interaction between inositol and GSK3beta, and highlighted the potential of inositol as a therapeutic prevention against lithium-induced embryonic neurotoxicity for childbearing female BPD patients.

title: Arecoline Induces Testicular Injury and Impairs Spermatogenesis in Rats Through Notch Signaling-Mediated Oxidative Stress.
authors: Yang, Yan-Qi; Li, Wen-Xing; Ge, Pan; Lv, Mo-Qi; Sun, Ying; Chen, Qing; Zhang, Jian; Sun, Rui-Fang; Zhou, Dang-Xia; Liu, Ming
abstract: Millions of people chew areca nut to boost work efficiency and relieve stress. Areca nut contains arecoline, which adversely affects reproductive function, although the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Herein, we evaluated arecoline-mediated reproductive toxicity using Sprague-Dawley (SD) rat models and an in vitro GC-1 cell model. Molecular docking, quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR), Western blot, cell-based assays, and functional rescue experiments were used to investigate the mechanisms involved. Dose-dependent spermatogenic damage was observed in male rats receiving 50, 100 and 200 mg/kg arecoline, with reduced sperm counts and quality, higher testicular MDA and lower activity of antioxidant enzymes superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and glutathione peroxidase (GPx). Molecular docking predicted a possible interaction between arecoline and Notch1. qRT-PCR and Western blot analyses showed that the expression of Notch1 and its ligands, Jagged-1 and Dll-1, was downregulated in testicular tissues and GC-1 cells following arecoline exposure. Notch1 expression was strongly positively correlated with seminiferous tubule diameter and seminiferous epithelium height. In vitro, arecoline induced ROS accumulation, inhibited proliferation and promoted apoptosis in GC-1 cells. Rescue experiments showed that the Notch activator valproic acid, used to enhance Notch signaling, alleviated arecoline-induced toxicity, whereas Notch inhibitor FLI-06 worsened cell injury. These findings support a role for altered Notch signaling and oxidative stress in arecoline-induced spermatogenic injury and provide insight into the molecular mechanisms of its reproductive toxicity.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic and Regulatory Network Analyses Identify a Putative HNF4A-OXR1 Association Linked to Podocyte Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
authors: Yang, Zhenkun; Jiang, Shimin; Cui, Wen; Zhou, Jiahui; Li, Wenge
abstract: Podocyte injury is a central pathological event in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), but the mitochondrial regulatory mechanisms underlying podocyte dysfunction remain incompletely defined. We integrated single-nucleus RNA-seq data from human renal biopsies in GSE195460 with podocyte-specific differential expression, functional enrichment, mitochondrial gene annotation, co-expression network analysis, machine learning feature selection, pseudotime analysis, in silico knockout, transcription factor enrichment, motif analysis, and molecular docking; findings were externally evaluated in GSE209781. Podocytes showed prominent disease-associated transcriptomic perturbation, with 677 exploratory cell-level differentially expressed genes and enrichment of cytoskeletal, adhesion, developmental, oxidative phosphorylation, and metabolic pathways. Thirty-one mitochondrial-related differentially expressed genes were identified, and OXR1 was prioritized as a candidate regulatory hub based on consistent downregulation, network centrality, machine learning selection, and external validation. HNF4A was predicted as an upstream regulator linked to OXR1 and other mitochondrial targets. In silico OXR1 perturbation increased the predicted injured-state probability from 15% to 82%, while promoter motif analysis provided additional computational support for a putative HNF4A-OXR1 regulatory relationship. These findings highlight OXR1 as a candidate associated with podocyte mitochondrial dysfunction in DKD and suggest a putative HNF4A-OXR1 regulatory relationship.

title: Discovery of Novel HDAC8 Inhibitors Through Shape-Based Virtual Screening: Experimental Validation and Characterization of a Promising Quinoline-Based Hit Scaffold.
authors: Gargano, Adriana; Gonzalez-Bakker, Aday; Puerta, Adrian; Maggisano, Valentina; Bulotta, Stefania; Rocca, Roberta; Padron, Jose M; Alcaro, Stefano
abstract: Histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) is overexpressed in several solid tumors and, unlike other Class I HDACs, functions independently of large corepressor complexes, making it an attractive target for structure-based drug design. Here, we aimed to identify novel natural compounds capable of targeting the human HDAC8 catalytic site. A library of 307,814 natural products from ZINC15 was screened by shape-based virtual screening using five structurally diverse co-crystallized HDAC8 ligands as templates, followed by molecular docking and Molecular Mechanics-Generalized Born Surface Area (MM-GBSA) binding free energy calculations. Seven commercially available hits were selected for enzymatic validation, leading to the identification of 4-((7-methoxyquinolin-4-yl)amino)benzamide (ZINC000054202375, compound 2) as a promising HDAC8 inhibitor. In vitro antiproliferative assays across multiple human solid tumor cell lines demonstrated significant growth inhibition by compound 2, further supported by colony formation assays. Mechanistic studies using label-free live-cell imaging, Annexin V staining, DAPI (4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole) nuclear morphology, and DCFDA (2',7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate) assays revealed membrane blebbing, mitotic failure, increased reactive oxygen species, and nuclear fragmentation, consistent with apoptosis induction. Finally, 1 mus molecular dynamics simulations supported the formation of a persistent ligand-receptor interaction network within the HDAC8 catalytic pocket. Overall, compound 2 represents a promising non-hydroxamate hit scaffold with promising HDAC8 inhibitory activity, serving as a starting point for the development of novel HDAC-targeted anticancer agents.

title: Regulatory Elements and Splicing Factors Govern Mutually Exclusive Splicing of DmRdl Exon 3.
authors: Song, Zijiao; Zhang, Yichi; Lin, Kaixiang; Wang, Xiugen; Duan, Yanan; Bao, Jian; Bass, Chris; Zhao, Chunqing
abstract: Ionotropic gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors are major inhibitory receptors in insect central nervous systems, with their diversity partly generated by alternative splicing. In Drosophila melanogaster, mutually exclusive alternative splicing (MEAS) of the resistant to dieldrin gene (Rdl) exon 3 (E3) produces Rdl-3a and Rdl-3b, but its regulatory mechanism remains unclear. In the present study, two intronic regulatory elements (IREs) and one exonic regulatory element (ERE) were identified in the exon 2 (E2)-exon 4 (E4) region of DmRdl precursor mRNA (pre-mRNA). The IRE1 mutation decreased exon 3b (E3b) inclusion from 54.12% to 3.95%, whereas the IRE2 mutation increased E3b inclusion from 61.70% to 97.82%. The ERE mutation significantly increased E3b inclusion both in vitro and in vivo, while the IRE mutations were lethal in vivo. The results of RNA pull-down, mass spectrometry, and RNAi demonstrated that the splicing factors, CG30122 and Rbp1-like bind to the ERE and exert opposite effects on E3b inclusion. The results of STRING network analysis supported the functional interaction between CG30122 and Rbp1-like, while molecular docking provided structural support for their potential interaction with the ERE-containing RNA sequence. This study reveals the molecular regulatory network underlying the MEAS of DmRdl E3, and and provides a foundation for investigating other MEAS exons, such as E6 and E9 in insect Rdl.

title: Genome-Wide Characterization of the CAMTA Gene Family in Paulownia fortunei and Potential Role of PfCAMTA5 in Salt-Stress Responses.
authors: Cao, Yabing; Sun, He; Liu, Chunyang; Liu, Jie; Cao, Shenquan; Zhao, Zhenli
abstract: Calmodulin-binding transcription activator (CAMTA) transcription factors play key roles in plant stress responses, but their functions in Paulownia fortunei remain largely unknown. Here, we identified eight CAMTA family genes in P. fortunei and investigated their structural features, evolutionary relationships, and expression patterns under salt stress. All PfCAMTA proteins contain the conserved CG-1, ANK, and IQ domains, although their gene structures and physicochemical properties differ. Phylogenetic and synteny analyses revealed close paralogous pairs and orthologous relationships with Arabidopsis CAMTAs. Under salt stress, the eight PfCAMTA genes displayed distinct tissue-specific expression patterns, with PfCAMTA5 emerging as the most prominent salt-responsive candidate, showing broad induction across tissues and the highest transcript abundance. Molecular docking and Y2H assays suggested a potential interaction between PfCAMTA5 and the salt-responsive calcium sensor PfCML28. Transient overexpression of PfCAMTA5 in tobacco improved salt tolerance, as reflected by enhanced photosynthesis, higher antioxidant enzyme activities, and reduced membrane damage, and up-regulation of stress-responsive genes. Together, these findings suggest that PfCAMTA5 may play a potential role in salt tolerance and provide a foundation for further investigation of the CAMTA-mediated salt stress regulatory network in P. fortunei.

title: Novel Palladium(II) beta-Diketonate Complexes: Synthesis, Dual Antimicrobial/Anticancer Activity, and Molecular Insights into DNA/Protein Interactions.
authors: Trifunovic Stevanovic, Marija; Joksimovic, Nenad; Petronijevic, Jelena; Stojanovic, Snezana; Dordevic, Sladana; Stankovic, Jelena Antic; Bufan, Biljana; Bozic, Dragana D
abstract: This study reports the synthesis and biological evaluation of four novel palladium(II) complexes (B1-B4) with O,O-bidentate beta-diketo ester ligands. Spectroscopic characterization confirmed their structures, while biological assays revealed substituent-dependent activity. Complexes B3 and B4 showed the most consistent antimicrobial activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of 312-1200 muM across the tested microorganisms. B3 exhibited the highest antiproliferative potency, with IC(50) values of 2.3, 5.2, and 5.4 muM against K-562, HeLa, and HaCaT cells, respectively. However, its selectivity varied with the cell model, reaching a selectivity index (SI) of 5.17 against K-562 cells relative to MRC-5 fibroblasts and 2.35 relative to HaCaT cells. B2 showed a more moderate activity profile, with some selectivity towards K-562 cells. Flow-cytometric analysis revealed increased sub-G0/G1 populations following treatment, consistent with the induction of apoptosis. Biophysical assays and molecular docking indicated structure-dependent interactions with DNA, while fluorescence studies revealed differences in the apparent binding affinities of the complexes toward human serum albumin (HSA). These findings highlight the influence of ligand structure on the biological activity and biomolecular interactions of palladium(II) complexes, identifying B3 as the most promising candidate for further investigation based on its antiproliferative potency and selectivity.

title: Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.
authors: Toumpe, Ilias; Masid, Maria; Hatzimanikatis, Vassily; Miskovic, Ljubisa
abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a subset of these candidates. All 28 emerged directly from the mechanistic model structure and multi-omics constraints, with no calibration to known drug targets or cancer-dependency data. Simulations of thymidylate synthase, hexokinase, and triokinase inhibition predicted target- and physiology-specific changes in pathway use, energy metabolism, and a shared ceramide-linked stress response. Mapping predicted enzyme-activity shifts to BRCA1-associated transcription factors suggested regulatory routes underlying differences between the two states. These ensembles provide a reusable framework for time-resolved, mechanistic hypothesis generation across cancers and other diseases. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

title: Computational and experimental analysis for the mismatched DNA recognition mechanism of TaqMutS.
authors: Jiang, Wenyan; Ding, Yiyang; Sun, Haojie; Li, Yuxuan; Liang, Xiao; Li, Quanshun
abstract: DNA holds great potential as a next-generation information storage material due to its high density, stability and low energy consumption. However, high synthesis errors severely limit its practical implementation. Enzymatic error correction based on Thermus aquaticus MutS (TaqMutS) is efficient and straightforward, whereas its severe non-specific binding to perfectly matched DNA drastically decreases the correction performance. In this work, we systematically analyzed the mechanism of mismatched DNA recognition by TaqMutS through alanine scanning mutagenesis, homologous substitution mutations and molecular dynamics simulations. The results revealed that TaqMutS recognized mismatched sites by sensing the local conformational strain of DNA. Specifically, a cooperative push-pull mechanism mediated by residues S57 and D472 modulated the pi-stacking interactions between the key recognition residue F39 and DNA. Meanwhile, the electrostatic synergistic effects of residues K61 and R473 effectively regulated the non-specific DNA binding of TaqMutS. Based on these findings, two mutants (V57S and K61H) were constructed, which exhibited enhanced binding efficiency for mismatched DNA and reduced affinity for perfectly matched DNA. Collectively, this study provided useful error-correction tools for high-efficiency DNA synthesis and laid an important theoretical foundation for the rational design of mismatched DNA recognition proteins.

title: Agnuside from Vitex negundo L. Attenuates Hepatocellular Lipid Accumulation: Association with the AMPK/SREBP1/FASN/HMGCR/PPARalpha/UCP2 Signaling Network.
authors: Saikia, Abhipsha; Ahmed, Semim Akhtar; Saikia, Kangkon; Sarma, Pranamika; Basumatary, Devi; Mukherjee, Ashis K; Borah, Jagat Chandra; Bala, Asis
abstract: Vitex negundo L. (VN) is a medicinal plant known for its anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective properties, commonly used as a vegetable in northeastern Indian communities. However, its role in treating nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is still underexplored. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of VN and its bioactive compounds in reducing lipid accumulation in CC1 hepatocytes. A crude extract of VN and its n-butanol fraction (VNBU) were tested on palmitate-induced CC1 hepatocytes to evaluate lipid accumulation. Key compounds Agnuside, 5-hydroxy-3,6,7,3́,4́-pentamethoxyflavone, and Vitexilactone were isolated. Agnuside's effects on lipogenesis, cholesterol accumulation, and fatty acid oxidation were assessed using biochemical assays and Western blot analysis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to explore its interactions with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR). Agnuside treatment was associated with reduced lipid accumulation by modulating Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), HMGCR, Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBP1), Fatty acid synthase (FASN), Peroxisome Proliferator-activated receptors (PPARalpha), and uncoupling protein (UCP2), suggesting a favorable shift in lipid metabolism. Computational studies indicated that Agnuside binds stably to HMGCR, similar to statins. In summary, these findings suggest that VN and Agnuside exert protective effects in hepatocytes, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism markers. Further studies are needed to confirm the causal role of this signaling network.

title: The protective role of apigenin against cadmium toxicity: study of metallothionein gene expression and antioxidant enzyme activity in mouse testicular tissue.
authors: Zarei, Zahra; Karimian, Mohammad; Davoodi, Parisa
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The present research explored how apigenin may exert a protective role against cadmium toxicity by evaluating the expression of metallothioneins (Mts) and metal regulatory transcription factor 1 (Mtf1) genes, along with assessing the activity of antioxidant enzymes Superoxide dismutase (Sod), Glutathione peroxidase (Gpx), and Catalase (Cat) in testicular tissue of male mice, followed by bioinformatics analysis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Within this experimental setup, male Balb/C mice received administration of cadmium and apigenin for 14 consecutive days. Mt1, Mt2, and Mtf1 gene expression, as well as Sod, Gpx, and Cat antioxidant enzyme activities, were measured in the testis. Molecular docking and gene network analysis were employed to investigate apigenin-metallothionein interactions and their associated gene connections. RESULTS: The expression of Mt1 and Mt2 genes was markedly elevated in the cadmium-treated group; however, apigenin administration significantly attenuated this up-regulation. In the case of Mtf1, cadmium exposure enhanced its expression, while apigenin exerted no noticeable effect. Moreover, cadmium treatment led to a reduction in the activity of Sod, Gpx, and Cat enzymes, whereas their activities were improved when apigenin was co-administered. Molecular docking revealed that apigenin interacted with both Mt1 and Mt2 proteins in the primary binding sites of the proteins. GeneMANIA revealed links between the three target genes and 20 others, mainly through physical interactions and co-expression, suggesting direct interaction and co-regulation. CONCLUSION: Apigenin can regulate the expression of metallothionein genes and preserve the activity of antioxidant enzymes Sod, Gpx, and Cat in mice subjected to cadmium exposure.

title: Integrative machine learning analysis of bulk and single-nucleus RNA sequencing reveals key cell types and biomarkers driving MASH-associated fibrosis.
authors: Zhang, Junjie; Wang, Junjie; Shen, Yan; Zhang, Yirong; Luo, Zimeng; Kong, Xinyao; Li, Wang; Luo, Juan; Xu, Fei; Wan, Shaogui
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) increases the risk of cirrhosis and liver cancer, with liver fibrosis being the primary determinant of adverse outcomes. However, the molecular mechanisms driving fibrosis progression in MASH remains incompletely understood. METHODS: We integrated four bulk RNA-seq datasets into a merged cohort (MergeCohort) and analyzed one single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) dataset. Robust Rank Aggregation (RRA), WGCNA and machine learning were combined to identify core genes associated with MASH fibrosis. Additionally, we established MASH mice model induced by methionine-choline-deficient (MCD) diet, and further check the expression of hub genes through quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Single-nucleus transcriptomic profiling of liver tissues from MASH patients across distinct fibrosis stages was investigated to delineate cellular heterogeneity, reconstruct intercellular communication networks, and characterize key transcription factors (TFs) as well as receptor-ligand interactions involved in MASH-associated fibrosis. RESULTS: Based on the MergeCohort, we detected two key gene network modules associated with fibrosis progression in MASH through WGCNA. By integrating machine learning algorithms, we discovered seven core genes (CAPN6, FAP, KRT23, SOX4, STMN2, TAGLN and VWF) showing favorable discriminatory capability for fibrosis stage, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.81 (95% CI 0.69-0.93) in a distinct external cohort. Moreover, CAPN6, FAP and KRT23 showed directionally consistent upregulation in the liver tissues of MASH mouse model induced by MCD diet. Subsequently, applying cell-type deconvolution analysis, we assigned the predominant cell types (hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), cholangiocytes, hepatocytes and macrophages) to the key WGCNA modules. At the single-nucleus level, we identified FGF13(+) cholangiocytes and SAAs(+) hepatocytes subpopulations. Transcription factor regulon analysis identified key TFs (CREB5 and STAT3), which may play potential regulatory roles in FGF13(+) cholangiocytes and SAAs(+) hepatocytes. Cell-cell communication analysis further revealed crucial ligand-receptor pairs between HSCs and FGF13(+) cholangiocytes (VEGFA_NRP1 and APP_CD74 axes), SAAs(+) hepatocytes and HSCs (RSPO3_LGR4 and IGF1_IGF1R axes), SAAs(+) hepatocytes and macrophages (TNFSF14_TNFRSF14 and SELE_CD44 axes) associated with the progression of liver fibrosis in MASH. CONCLUSION: This combined approach defines molecular signatures related to MASH fibrosis that may inform the development of novel therapeutic strategies and serve as a tissue signature associated with advanced fibrosis in MASH.

title: ELF3 (E74 like ETS transcription factor 3) promotes tumor growth and autophagy in pancreatic cancer.
authors: Shang, Yuru; Zhang, Pingping; Yang, Yanhui; Fan, Yibao; Yang, Zhichao; Sun, Hongshi; Wang, Jia; Yu, Zhengming; Wu, Jiale; Wang, Wenxu; Kahlert, Ulf Dietrich; Sethi, Gautam; Linnebacher, Michael; Chen, Zhe-Sheng; Klionsky, Daniel J; Zhang, Xianbin
journal: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the research progress of the past decades, the prognosis for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains poor. Identifying novel targets and exploring the underlying mechanisms is therefore of great importance. ELF3 (E74 like ETS transcription factor 3) is a member of the E-twenty-six (ETS) family and previous studies suggest that ELF3 may play a promoting role in malignant epithelial tumor; however, the effect and exact mechanism have not been determined in pancreatic cancer. METHODS: ELF3 expression and its prognostic relevance in pancreatic cancer were analyzed using clinical datasets. The role of ELF3 in autophagy regulation was evaluated using molecular and cellular approaches in vitro and in vivo. Computer-aided drug design was performed to identify potential ELF3 inhibitors, whose anti-tumor efficacy was subsequently evaluated. RESULTS: In the present study, it is observed that high expression of ELF3 leads to a poor overall survival in pancreatic cancer patients. Functional experiments demonstrated that knockdown of ELF3 blocks autophagy. In addition, SRT2183 was identified as a potential ELF3 inhibitor using molecular docking. In vitro and in vivo results showed that SRT2183 blocks autophagy and exerts anti-carcinoma effect. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that ELF3 promotes autophagy through transcriptional regulation of ATG10 and identify ELF3 as a potential therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer. SRT2183, an ELF3-targeting compound that suppresses autophagic flux and tumor growth, represents a promising candidate for further therapeutic development.

title: IGF2BP3 promotes M2 macrophage polarization and ESCC progression by increasing USP36-mediated beta-catenin stabilization.
authors: Tian, Zhongxian; Zhou, Yongjia; Zhao, Yunpeng; Li, Peiwei; Ding, Yi; Tang, Guoshuo; Zhao, Yunfei; Cui, Qingkun; Li, Peichao; Pedersen, Lotte Bang; Jiang, Ning; Wu, Honglei; Zhao, Xiaogang
abstract: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is a highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis that is characterized by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that critically contributes to tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. RNA-binding proteins are emerging regulators of cancer biology; however, their role in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the function and mechanism of the RNA-binding protein IGF2BP3 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression and immune modulation. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets including esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and adjacent normal tissues were integrated to identify dysregulated RNA-binding proteins. The functional role of IGF2BP3 was evaluated using in vitro assays, organoid models, and immunocompetent and immunodeficient mouse models. RNA immunoprecipitation, polysome profiling, ubiquitination assays, and luciferase reporter assays were employed to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Immune cell infiltration was analyzed by flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunofluorescence. Virtual screening, biolayer interferometry, and molecular docking were used to identify small-molecule inhibitors of IGF2BP3. Statistical analyses included Student's t tests, one-way analysis of variance, Kaplan‒Meier survival analysis, and correlation analyses. RESULTS: IGF2BP3 was specifically overexpressed in epithelial tumor cells, exhibited progressively increasing expression during esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression, and correlated with poor clinical outcomes. IGF2BP3 promoted tumor growth by activating Wnt signaling through the stabilization of beta-catenin. Mechanistically, IGF2BP3 increased the translation of the deubiquitinase USP36 without altering the stability of its messenger RNA, leading to the USP36-mediated deubiquitination and stabilization of beta-catenin. Activation of beta-catenin signaling increased the transcription and secretion of transforming growth factor beta, which promoted the polarization of macrophages toward the immunosuppressive M2 phenotype. Pharmacological inhibition of IGF2BP3 with digoxin disrupted the IGF2BP3-USP36-beta-catenin axis, reduced transforming growth factor beta production, suppressed tumor growth, and increased the efficacy of paclitaxel and PD-1 blockade in preclinical models. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies IGF2BP3 as a critical posttranscriptional regulator that links oncogenic signaling to immune suppression in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Targeting IGF2BP3 represents a promising therapeutic strategy to remodel the tumor microenvironment and improve responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

title: Circuit-aligned specialization of human basal ganglia astrocytes.
authors: Fu, Yuanyuan; Kempynck, Niklas; Ding, Wubin; Turner, Meghan A; Garcia, Aaron D; Schmitz, Matthew T; Close, Jennie; Kapen, Inkar; Hewitt, Madeleine; Seeman, Stephanie C; Long, Brian; Ding, Song-Lin; Ho, Windy; Mahoney, Joseph T; Mich, John K; Levi, Boaz P; Klein, Amit; Behrens, Maria Margarita; Ecker, Joseph; Aerts, Stein; Johansen, Nelson J; Hodge, Rebecca D; Lein, Ed S; Bakken, Trygve E
abstract: Astrocytes shape synapses and circuits, yet their diversity within the human basal ganglia remains poorly defined. Integrating single-nucleus transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with spatial transcriptomics, we identify three anatomically organized astrocyte subgroups-striatal gray matter (GM), extra-striatal GM, and white matter (WM)-distinguished by neurotransmitter transporter expression and synapse-associated programs that reflect afferent input. These molecular distinctions generalize brain-wide, separating telencephalic from non-telencephalic astrocytes, with LHX2 marking telencephalic astrocyte identity across species. Within the striatum (STR), dorsal and ventral populations align with distinct microcircuits; a ventral population maps to the nucleus accumbens mediodorsal shell alongside specialized neuronal subtypes, a pattern conserved in nonhuman primates. A deep learning sequence model identifies subgroup-specific enhancer codes and recovers established transcription factor motif logic from published enhancer-AAV datasets, providing a foundation for targeted viral vector design. These findings define intersecting axes of human astrocyte specialization and offer a framework for cell-type-specific dissection of basal ganglia circuits.

title: Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia.
authors: Chang, Lei; Li, Kai; Xie, Yang; Zhong, Guojie; Rink, Jonathan A; Baez-Becerra, Cindy Tatiana; Lie, Audrey; Indralingam, Hannah S; Loe, Timothy; Dong, Keyi; Gao, Xiaomeng; Wang, Zhaoning; Zu, Songpeng; Kern, Joseph Colin; Zhao, Zoey; Boone, Eric; Flores, Jesus; Monell, Alexander; Olness, Jacqueline; Barragan, Cesar; Osgood, Emma; Owens, William; Schenker-Ahmed, Natalie; Zhang, Wenjin; Liu, Di; Barcoma, Ariana S; Willier, Jackson K; Knutson, Kyle W; Russo, Kaitlyn G; Liu, Jiayi; Cho, Silvia; Arzavala, Jessica; Young, Carissa K; Sundaram, Guha V; Manning, Austin C; Sanchez, Yareli; Bikkina, Aleksandra; Berry, Jillian V; O'Connor, Carolyn; Liem, Michelle; Marrin, Mikayla V; Rose, Cynthia; Alt, Shane N; Zhu, Chenxu; Zemke, Nathan R; Ding, Wubin; Klein, Amit; Fu, Yuanyuan; Johansen, Nelson; Bakken, Trygve E; Hodge, Rebecca D; Keene, C Dirk; Lein, Ed S; Li, Daofeng; Zhu, Quan; Wang, Ting; Xu, Xiangmin; Ecker, Joseph R; Behrens, M Margarita; Ren, Bing
abstract: The basal ganglia are central to motor control, learning, emotion, and reward processing, and their dysfunction contributes to many neurological and psychiatric disorders. Here, we generated a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical human donors. This atlas resolved cell-type- and region-specific landscapes of active and repressive candidate cis-regulatory elements and delineated gene regulatory networks underlying cell identity. We found that the combinatorial expression of homeobox transcription factors provides distinctive molecular descriptors of neuronal cell identities in the basal ganglia. Integration with matched MERFISH spatial transcriptomics further uncovered regional heterogeneity in epigenomic and transcriptional programs. Finally, we used this atlas to interpret noncoding risk variants associated with neuropsychiatric disorders and to construct a deep-learning model that predicts gene regulatory activities and variant effects. Together, this work provides a multimodal regulatory framework for understanding human basal ganglia organization, evolution, and disease genetics.

title: Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.
authors: Bani Saadat, Hossein; Vaez Torshizi, Rasoul; Masoudi, Ali Akbar
abstract: Identifying associations between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and economically important traits is fundamental to modern poultry breeding programs. However, genome-wide studies based on commercial high-density SNP arrays are often prohibitively expensive, particularly for large populations and in resource-limited settings. Therefore, this study employed a cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) approach combined with two ensemble machine learning algorithms, Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), to identify informative markers of body weight (BW) at hatch, 3 weeks (BW3), and 6 weeks (BW6) of age in broiler chickens derived from reciprocal crosses between the commercial Arian line and native Urmia chicken. A total of 368 birds were genotyped using GBS, and 312 second-generation (F(2)) birds with complete phenotypic records were utilized for genomic screening and machine learning analyses. The hyperparameters of both machine learning algorithms were optimized using a grid search with three-fold cross-validation. The combined application of RF and GBM identified several informative SNP markers located on chromosomes 1, 4, 13, 17, 19, 20, and 24. Positional candidate genes located within these genomic regions included platelet-derived growth factor D (PDGFD), KIRRE-like nephrin family adhesion molecule 3 (KIRREL3), ETS proto-oncogene 1, transcription factor (ETS1), acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 1 (ACSL1), diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 2 (DGAT2), and selenophosphate synthetase 1 (SEPHS1). Gene Ontology enrichment analysis indicated that these genes are involved in biological processes related to the regulation of protein degradation, immune responses, and lipid metabolism. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating cost-effective GBS with machine learning approaches to identify genomic regions and informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens, providing valuable genomic resources for future breeding and genetic improvement programs.

title: Integrated in silico assessment of the regulatory and structural consequences of pulmonary tuberculosis-associated SP110 polymorphisms.
authors: Kyabaggu, Denis S; Ssekagiri, Alfred; Katagirya, Eric; Bagaya, Bernard S; Joloba, Moses L; Andia-Biraro, Irene; Kateete, David Patrick; Mayanja-Kizza, Harriet; Nakiyingi, Lydia
abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying conflicting findings of association of SP110 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with susceptibility to pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) remain unclear. We selected ten SP110 SNPs from publicly available genomic databases, based on prior PTB association and minor allele frequencies exceeding 1% in African populations and identified in a Ugandan cohort with PTB. We then applied in silico multi-tool framework, incorporating deep-learning splice predictors including SpliceAI, Pangolin, and AlphaGenome, to evaluate the regulatory and functional consequences of the SNPs on transcription factor binding, RNA splicing, RNA secondary structure, and protein-level effects. The model captured population-relevant SP110 variations rather than a directly genotyped Ugandan cohort. Our analysis revealed allele-specific gains and losses involving transcription factors TFAP2A, TFAP2C, TP63, Zfx, and IRF1, suggesting modulation of regulatory potential through altered transcription factor binding motifs. However, SpliceAI and Pangolin uniformly predicted low splice-disruptive effects across both exonic and intronic variants, while multiple protein pathogenicity tools consistently classified missense and stop-gained variants as benign or tolerated. RNA secondary structure analysis predicted that most variants preserved global thermodynamic stability. From our findings, SP110 variants are unlikely to exert major effects through splicing disruption or protein destabilization but may contribute to functional diversity through subtle regulatory mechanisms, including transcription factor binding modulation and RNA structural reorganization. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-65881-y.

title: A noninvasive risk stratification prediction model for neuroblastoma through integration of multidimensional clinical indicators.
authors: Zhang, Mengxin; Zhang, Yingyu; Zhang, Xianwei; Zhao, Liang; Wu, Yuxuan; Zhang, Man; Ren, Jianying; Wu, Yongjun; Zhang, Jie; Zhang, Wancun
abstract: Current neuroblastoma (NB) risk classification relies partly on tumor tissue-derived information, which may be unavailable in patients who cannot undergo biopsy or surgical resection. Therefore, this study aimed to develop a non-invasive prediction model for NB risk classification by integrating a liquid biopsy biomarker with routinely available clinical indicators. A total of 141 treatment-naive patients with NB were included and divided into a training cohort (n = 100) and a held-out testing cohort (n = 41). Six pretreatment predictors, including age, sex, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), neuron-specific enolase (NSE), image-defined risk factors (IDRFs), and circulating plasma MYCN amplification status, were incorporated into 11 machine-learning algorithms. Model development and selection were performed exclusively in the training cohort using repeated nested cross-validation with patient-level out-of-fold predictions. Random forest (RF) achieved the best overall performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.952 (95% CI, 0.906-0.998), an accuracy of 91%, and a Brier score of 0.079. Decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit across the prespecified threshold range of 15%-50%, while SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis identified IDRFs, NSE, and LDH as the leading contributors to model predictions. After model locking, the RF model retained good discrimination in the held-out testing cohort, with an AUC of 0.890 (95% CI, 0.791-0.989), a sensitivity of 84.2%, and a Brier score of 0.140. CONCLUSION: These findings support the feasibility of combining circulating MYCN status with routine clinical variables to provide a non-tissue-based approach for assisting NB risk classification. WHAT IS KNOWN: * Current NB risk classification incorporates clinical, imaging, histopathological, and molecular information, some of which requires tumor tissue and may be unavailable before biopsy or surgery. WHAT IS NEW: * This study developed and independently tested a non-invasive machine-learning model integrating circulating plasma MYCN amplification status with five routinely available clinical indicators, achieving an AUC of 0.952 during nested cross-validation in the training cohort and an AUC of 0.890 in the held-out testing cohort.

title: Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture Alleviates Knee Osteoarthritis via Inhibition of TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB Signaling and Is Associated With Gut Microbiota Alterations.
authors: Wu, Jin; Wen, Zhi; Ye, Zifeng; Qiu, Liguo; Xia, Guang; Tan, Xuyi; Guo, Tikang; Tang, Yong; Lu, Min; Xu, Xiaotong; Kuang, Gaoyan
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the chondroprotective effects of Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture (JDJM) in KOA and to determine whether JDJM modulates the TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB axis and is associated with gut microbiota alterations. METHODS: A KOA model was established in New Zealand rabbits using a modified Videman method (n = 36). Animals were assigned to a blank control group (n = 6) or underwent modeling and were then randomized into the model, JDJM low-, medium-, or high-dose, and positive control groups (n = 6/group). Treatments were administered intragastrically for 6 weeks. Cartilage histopathology, evaluated by H&E staining and OARSI scoring, constituted the primary histopathological assessment, with the OARSI score serving as the quantitative primary endpoint. Secondary mechanistic outcomes included serum inflammatory cytokines and TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB-related measures in cartilage tissue, including NF-kappaB p65 nuclear translocation. In vitro, primary rabbit chondrocytes were exposed to IL-1beta-induced inflammatory stimulation to provide supportive mechanistic evidence through assessment of cell viability, apoptosis, inflammatory mediators, and pathway-related molecules. Molecular docking was additionally performed to explore potential interactions between identified JDJM constituents and TLR4/MD-2, MyD88, and NF-kappaB p65. Fecal 16S rRNA sequencing and related gut microbiota analyses were considered exploratory. RESULTS: Compared with the model group, JDJM attenuated cartilage histopathological damage and reduced OARSI scores, while decreasing serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha, and IFN-gamma). In cartilage tissue, JDJM reduced TLR4, MyD88, and NF-kappaB expression and suppressed NF-kappaB p65 nuclear translocation. In vitro, JDJM increased the viability of IL-1beta-stimulated chondrocytes, reduced apoptosis, and decreased the release of inflammatory mediators. Molecular docking revealed distinct docking profiles of JDJM constituents against TLR4/MD-2, MyD88, and NF-kappaB p65. 16S rRNA sequencing indicated a shift in gut microbiota composition in the KOA model. Following JDJM treatment, microbiota composition was modulated, and several bacterial genera showed significant correlations with inflammatory markers and pathway-related molecules. CONCLUSION: JDJM exerted anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective effects in in vivo KOA models and in vitro primary chondrocytes. These effects may be mediated, at least in part, by inhibition of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB signaling axis. The observed microbiota changes suggest that the gut-joint axis may contribute to the overall effects, although causal relationships require further validation.

title: Shenfu Injection attenuates isoproterenol-induced heart failure partly through modulation of the TNF-alpha/TNFR1/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Wang, Zhiqiang; Zhao, Zhenyu; Li, Weijun; Hu, Zhixi; Ye, Jiahao
abstract: Shenfu injection (SFI) is widely used for heart failure (HF), but its cardioprotective mechanism remains incompletely understood. In this study, an isoproterenol-induced HF rat model, H9c2 cell injury model, network pharmacology, GEO analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were integrated to explore the mechanism of SFI. In rats, SFI improved cardiac function, with the medium-dose group increasing LVEF from 62.03 +/- 5.89% in the ISO group to 79.33 +/- 2.62% and LVFS from 29.68 +/- 3.97% to 43.03 +/- 2.49%. SFI also reduced NT-proBNP, inflammatory cytokines, and myocardial apoptosis. In H9c2 cells, 4 per thousand SFI improved ISO-induced cell injury and reduced apoptosis and inflammatory responses. Network pharmacology and GEO analysis indicated enrichment of the TNF signaling pathway, and molecular simulation suggested potential interactions between candidate SFI-related compounds and targets in the TNF-alpha/TNFR1/NF-kappaB axis. These findings suggest that SFI attenuates HF-related cardiac injury partly by suppressing inflammation and apoptosis through modulation of the TNF-alpha/TNFR1/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.

title: P53-assisted METTL14-mediated m(6)A modification of SLC7A11 drives ferroptosis and inflammation in polycystic ovary syndrome.
authors: Chen, Xiaohong; Lin, Jing; Ning, Peng; Liu, Dekun; Zhang, Ruibing; Chi, Zhoulin; Zeng, Yahan; Yu, Zheng; Yu, Shuguang; Yang, Sha
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by chronic inflammation and follicular arrest, yet the molecular drivers linking these pathologies to granulosa cell (GC) death remain elusive. Here, we identify a ferroptosis-inflammation cascade as a critical determinant of ovarian dysfunction in PCOS. We demonstrate that the N(6)-methyladenosine (m(6)A) methyltransferase METTL14 is aberrantly upregulated in human PCOS GCs, correlating with oxidative damage. Mechanistically, we uncover a non-canonical paradigm where upregulated P53 functions as an essential RNA-binding cofactor, recruiting METTL14 to the SLC7A11 transcript. Validated by AlphaFold3 modeling, this METTL14-p53 complex catalyzes SLC7A11 m(6)A hypermethylation and mRNA destabilization. The resulting SLC7A11 deficiency dismantles antioxidant defenses, driving ferroptosis and amplifying local inflammation. Crucially, in a DHEA-induced PCOS rat model, genetic ablation of Tp53 severed this pathogenic axis, restoring redox balance, suppressing inflammation, and reversing the polycystic phenotype. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal epigenetic mechanism linking m(6)A reprogramming, iron-dependent cell death, and inflammation, highlighting the METTL14-p53-SLC7A11 axis as a therapeutic target in PCOS.

title: Impaired IFN-gamma/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.
authors: Li, Zhuojun; Li, Jing; Chen, Xixi; Liu, Yehai
abstract: 4-Nonylphenol (4-NP) is a persistent endocrine-disrupting chemical, but its role in allergic rhinitis (AR) remains poorly understood. The study here integrated human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and experimental validation to investigate the mechanisms underlying 4-NP-aggravated AR. Network analysis identified four shared candidates, e.g., CDKN1A, SKIL, IFNG, and B4GALT1. In an independent cohort, IFNG and SKIL were down-regulated in AR, whereas CDKN1A was increased. Single-cell analysis showed that IFNG was mainly expressed in T-cells. Molecular docking predicted the strongest interaction between 4-NP and IFNgamma (-6.4 kcal/mol), and a 50-ns molecular dynamics simulation supported the stability of the predicted complex. In human nasal epithelial progenitor cells (HNEPC), 4-NP increased IL1B, TNF, and IL6 expression. In house dust mite (HDM)-induced AR mice, 4-NP co-exposure increased nasal rubbing, eosinophilic inflammation, T(H)2 responses, IL-4 production, and inflammatory gene expression, while reducing Ifng expression, T(H)1 cells, and STAT1 phosphorylation. Recombinant IFNgamma partially reversed the T(H)1/T(H)2 imbalance and reduced eosinophilic inflammation and IL-4 levels. These findings suggest that 4-NP aggravates AR in association with impaired IFNgamma/STAT1-related immune regulation and enhanced nasal epithelial inflammation.

title: 27-Hydroxycholesterol Modulates Microglial alpha-Synuclein Handling and Is Associated with AKT1/JAK-STAT/TNF Signaling in Parkinson's Disease Models.
authors: Wei, LiWei; Tang, Shuangfeng; Li, Guozhi; Hua, Junkai; Tang, Xiangzhu; Lei, Jianming; Wei, Lijian
abstract: 27-Hydroxycholesterol (27-OHC) is an oxysterol implicated in neuroinflammation, but its relationship to microglial alpha-synuclein (alpha-syn) handling and intracellular signaling in Parkinson's disease (PD) models remains incompletely defined. We combined BV2-cell assays, an rAAV-A53T mouse model, untargeted lipidomics and proteomics, network analyses, molecular docking, pathway immunoblotting, pharmacological AKT inhibition, and a cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). In BV2 cells, 0.5-2.5 muM 27-OHC did not reduce viability, whereas concentrations >/= 5 muM were cytotoxic. At 2.5 muM, 27-OHC increased cell-associated alpha-syn signal after exposure to recombinant alpha-syn PFFs. Brain lipidomics in the PD model showed accumulation of the broad sterol-lipid class, but did not provide absolute brain 27-OHC concentrations. Network analyses nominated AKT1, IL6, STAT3, and MMP9 as hub genes. In three independent BV2 experiments, PFF and 27-OHC exposure were associated with altered phosphorylation of AKT, STAT3, and NF-kappaB p65; a PFF x 27-OHC interaction was detected for STAT3 phosphorylation. MK-2206 lowered the cell-associated alpha-syn/GAPDH signal in the combined-treatment group, although the comparison did not remain significant after adjustment across three pairwise tests. CETSA showed greater soluble AKT1 retention after 27-OHC exposure and a higher thermal-curve area under the curve (paired p = 0.023). These findings support an association between 27-OHC exposure, microglial alpha-syn handling, and AKT-related signaling in BV2 cells. They do not establish direct 27-OHC-AKT1 binding or an in vivo causal effect of brain 27-OHC on microglia.

title: Comprehensive identification of lactate metabolism-related genes in recurrent spontaneous abortion: An observational study integrating bioinformatics and experimental validation.
authors: Tang, Daili; Chen, Lin; Zheng, Huiling; Huang, Zhi; Lai, Ting
abstract: Recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) is a complex multifactorial disease. Lactate metabolism (LM) has been implicated in RSA pathogenesis, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This observational study aimed to identify key LM-related genes (LM-RGs) in RSA and explore their potential regulatory mechanisms and therapeutic targets. The study combined bioinformatics analysis with experimental validation. The training dataset GSE26787 and validation dataset GSE165004 were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. Differentially expressed genes were identified using the limma package. Candidate LM-RGs were obtained by intersecting differentially expressed genes with 262 LM-RGs from the Gene Set Enrichment Analysis database. Hub genes were identified through protein-protein interaction network analysis using the CytoHubba plugin (National Cheng Kung University). Key genes were further screened using Boruta and random forest machine learning algorithms, followed by expression validation in both Gene Expression Omnibus datasets. Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction was performed on 10 RSA and 10 control endometrial samples to validate key gene expression. Gene set enrichment analysis and gene set variation analysis were conducted to explore functional pathways. Regulatory networks involving microRNAs, long noncoding RNAs, and transcription factors were constructed, and potential therapeutic drugs were predicted using the Drug Signatures Database. CALR (upregulated) and PIEZO1 (downregulated) were identified as key genes in RSA and were functionally linked to pathways such as cytokine signaling. Furthermore, we delineated a regulatory network governing these genes, implicating the long noncoding RNA X-inactive specific transcript and shared transcription factors, including MYC proto-oncogene, bHLH transcription factor and vitamin D receptor. We propose several candidate drugs, including estradiol, predicted to target both CALR and PIEZO1. This study identifies CALR and PIEZO1 as key LM-RGs in RSA, with significant dysregulation confirmed in clinical samples. These genes are involved in cytokine signaling pathways and are regulated by complex molecular networks. The identification of common targeting drugs provides a foundation for developing novel therapeutic strategies for RSA. Further studies are warranted to validate these findings and explore their clinical applications.

title: 20(S)-Protopanaxadiol Targets HMGB1 to Inhibit Inflammasome Activation and Ameliorate Acute Lung Injury.
authors: Li, Junyao; Li, Jing; Dai, Jiawei; Hu, Jianping; Wang, Yuhan; Yan, Pengrui; Wang, Honggang; Hu, Weicheng
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: 20(S)-Protopanaxadiol (PPD), a major intestinal metabolite of ginsenosides from Panax ginseng, possesses anti-inflammatory properties, yet its direct molecular targets are poorly defined. This study investigated the protective effects of PPD against acute lung injury (ALI) and its potential mechanism. Using LPS-challenged immortalized mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages (iBMDMs) and ALI mouse models, limited proteolysis-mass spectrometry identified HMGB1 as the primary binding target. PPD blocked inflammasome activation and interrupted HMGB1-TLR4 interaction. Molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and site mutagenesis verified that PPD stably binds the HMGB1 B-box domain. In vivo, PPD mitigated pulmonary damage, alleviated alveolar edema and inflammatory infiltration, lowered proinflammatory cytokines, and restrained HMGB1 secretion. In conclusion, PPD directly targets HMGB1 to block HMGB1-TLR4 inflammatory signaling. These data suggest PPD can serve as a promising functional food constituent for ALI prevention.

title: Targeting TLR2 to Overcome Autophagy-Dependent Chemoresistance in Gastric Cancer: Integrating Molecular Docking, Mechanistic Validation, and Therapeutic Evaluation.
authors: Zheng, Kuanheng; Lei, Xinjian; Lin, Bin; Yang, Qianhong; He, Cong; Gao, Jin; Li, Feng
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
abstract: Chemoresistance remains a major barrier to effective treatment of gastric cancer (GC), particularly in advanced disease, where cytotoxic chemotherapy often yields limited and transient responses. The present study provides integrated computational and experimental evidence that targeting TLR2 using repurposed small-molecule inhibitors can overcome autophagy-dependent chemoresistance in gastric adenocarcinoma cells. A library comprising 1555 FDA-approved drugs was sourced from the DrugBank database, virtual screening was executed, and two compounds, Nilotinib (DB04868) and Lomitapide (DB08827), achieved affinities </= -10 kcal/mol. Chemoresistant GC cells were developed, and experimental assessment was performed using cell proliferation assay, apoptosis assay, real-time PCR, and western blot analysis. Nilotinib and Lomitapide significantly reduced the proliferation but increased the apoptosis of chemoresistant GC cells. Additionally, Nilotinib and lomitapide reduced the mRNA and protein levels of autophagy-related factors, LC3B, Beclin-1, and p62/SQSTM1, and activated transcription factors in chemoresistant GC cells. In conclusion, our results suggest that combining TLR2-targeted agents with standard chemotherapy could be a promising strategy to overcome refractory disease in GC.

title: scMINA: an interpretable workflow for paired scRNA-scATAC multiome integration and regulatory prioritization.
authors: Zhang, Shuwen; Hu, Hongru; Wang, Xue; Xiong, Chengjie; Kanekiyo, Takahisa; Asmann, Yan W; Ren, Yingxue
abstract: Single-cell multiomic technologies that jointly profile transcriptomic and epigenomic states provide unprecedented opportunities to investigate cellular heterogeneity and gene regulatory mechanisms in complex diseases. However, analysis of paired single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) data remains computationally challenging due to modality-specific technical variation, integration complexity, and limited interpretability of downstream regulatory inference. Here, we present scMINA (single-cell Multimodal Integration and Network Attribution), a modular and interpretable analytical workflow for the analysis of paired single-cell multiome datasets. scMINA comprises coordinated modules for multimodal integration, technical covariate correction, and regulatory feature prioritization, enabling systematic characterization of cellular states across transcriptomic and epigenomic modalities. In addition, scMINA incorporates explainable artificial intelligence-based attribution strategies to prioritize candidate genes and transcription factors associated with cell-state heterogeneity and disease-related regulatory alterations. We applied scMINA to the single-cell multiome data from the Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas, where the workflow robustly resolved major glial cell populations and identified regulatory features associated with Alzheimer's disease pathology. By coupling multimodal integration with interpretable regulatory prioritization, scMINA provides a practical workflow for systematic analysis and biological interpretation of paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq datasets.

title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations Indicate Inhibitor-Induced Closure of the TEAD-YAP Interface 2.
authors: Kaiser, Jesko; Gunera, Jakub; Heinrich, Timo
abstract: The interaction of TEAD with its cofactor YAP plays a crucial role in cancer. Several inhibitors have been described as binding to the P-site of TEAD, without directly interacting with the TEAD-YAP interfaces. However, the mechanism of action of those inhibitors remains not fully understood. In this study, we conducted an extensive analysis of available X-ray structures and found that allosteric effects of cocrystalized inhibitors in TEAD cannot be explained by the static information provided by these experimental structures. We then performed molecular dynamics simulations, which are consistent with inhibitors populating a closed conformation in between Y361 and S328, located at the YAP-TEAD binding interface 2. This effect is consistent among different inhibitors and different TEAD subtypes. Our simulations also suggest that YAP binding appears to be associated with the opening of this region, consistent with the effect of palmitic acid. These results support the hypothesis that P-site binders not only restrict protein dynamics but may also inhibit YAP binding by allosterically modulating YAP-TEAD interface 2.

title: Tiliroside reverses cisplatin resistance in non-small cell lung cancer via targeting IL-17RA to downregulate JAK2/STAT3 signaling.
authors: Zhang, Guanqing; Wang, Xinhao; Wang, Yue; Liu, Huan; Xie, Qiqiang; Li, Xin; Xu, Maolei; Zhou, Ling
journal: The Journal of pharmacy and pharmacology
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cisplatin resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is closely associated with inflammation. This study investigates whether tiliroside, a bioactive flavonoid exhibiting potent anti-inflammatory properties, can sensitize both NSCLC and its cisplatin-resistant variants to cisplatin treatment. METHODS: The reversal of cisplatin resistance and synergistic interactions between tiliroside and cisplatin were evaluated in vitro using cell proliferation, apoptosis, and comet assays, and in vivo via mouse xenograft models. Underlying mechanisms were elucidated through transcriptomic analysis and rescue experiments, while direct target engagement was characterized using molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assays, and biolayer interferometry. KEY FINDINGS: Tiliroside synergistically reversed both intrinsic and acquired cisplatin resistance in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulated IL-17A and IL-17RA expression, alongside activated IL-17 signaling, in cisplatin-resistant A549 cells. Target investigations demonstrated that tiliroside directly binds to IL-17RA, downregulating its expression and subsequently inhibiting the downstream IL-17/JAK2/STAT3 pathway. Furthermore, human recombinant IL-17A and IL-6 counteracted the inhibitory effects of tiliroside on STAT3 activation and its ability to enhance cisplatin sensitivity. CONCLUSIONS: IL-17RA represents a promising clinical target for overcoming cisplatin resistance in NSCLC. Tiliroside could serve as a valuable chemosensitizer by directly targeting IL-17RA to inhibit JAK2/STAT3 signaling.

title: Eupalinolide I derivative EJM alleviates experimental hyperuricemia through STAT1-associated regulation of intestinal inflammation and gut microbiota.
authors: Yan, Lilin; Zhu, Zhimin; Xu, Yuanjian; Lin, Yudong; Xu, Zhaohui; Zhou, Mingmei
journal: The Journal of pharmacy and pharmacology
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperuricemia (HUA) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder involving metabolic dysregulation and chronic inflammation, with emerging evidence implicating the intestine as a key extra-renal site of urate handling. However, the molecular mechanisms linking intestinal inflammation, urate transport, and immune signaling in HUA remain incompletely understood. AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the anti-hyperuricemic effects of EJM, a synthetic derivative of eupalinolide I, and to explore its potential mechanisms with a particular focus on intestinal inflammation, urate transport, and immune-related signaling pathways. METHODS: HUA was induced in mice using potassium oxonate, yeast extract, and fructose. The effects of EJM were assessed via serum biochemistry, histopathology, Western blotting, and 16S rRNA sequencing. The direct target of EJM was identified using human proteome microarray and validated by cellular thermal shift assay and molecular docking. RESULTS: EJM significantly reduced serum uric acid levels and alleviated renal and intestinal pathological injury in hyperuricemic mice. Proteome microarray screening, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assay supported STAT1 as a binding target of EJM. EJM treatment was associated with attenuation of intestinal IFN-gamma/JAK/STAT1 pathway activation and reduced levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IFN-gamma, IL-17A, IL-6, and TNF-alpha. These changes were accompanied by coordinated regulation of urate transporters: EJM downregulated renal URAT1 and GLUT9, reduced intestinal GLUT9, and upregulated ABCG2 in both kidney and intestine, thereby favoring urate excretion. In addition, EJM treatment partially reversed HUA-associated gut microbiota dysbiosis, with changes in microbial taxa related to intestinal inflammation and urate metabolism. CONCLUSION: EJM exhibits anti-hyperuricemic activity in experimental HUA. The findings suggest that STAT1-associated intestinal inflammatory regulation and urate transport modulation may contribute to its pharmacological effects, with gut microbiota changes occurring in parallel. Further functional validation is required to establish the causal roles of STAT1 signaling and microbiota remodeling.

title: Predicting Ternary Complex Stability through Binding Free-Energy Calculations in the Geometric Route.
authors: Tan, Benedict; Ciulli, Alessio; Michel, Julien
journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
abstract: Molecular glue-induced targeted protein degradation is a powerful emerging therapeutic modality that exploits the ubiquitin-proteasome degradation pathway to break down proteins associated with disease proliferation. At the structural level, degradation proceeds through the formation of a ternary complex induced by small molecules between the target protein and an E3 ligase. Unlike PROTACs, molecular glues do not require a chemical linker and tend to stabilize preexisting native protein-protein interactions. Computational screening of novel glues is challenging, in large part due to the complexity and high degree of cooperativity involved in the formation of the ternary complex interface. Here, we present a rigorous Molecular Dynamics-based simulation protocol that uses Umbrella Sampling to calculate the ternary complex binding free energy. The protocol follows a geometric thermodynamic cycle with conformational and Boresch-style orientational restraints to drive the system from bound to unbound. Our framework successfully predicts the effect of single-point interface mutations on the relative stability of the CK1alpha-lenalidomide-CRBN ternary complex (R2 = 0.95 compared to experimental binding affinities). We also study a series of systems related to the BRD4 degraders IBG1 and IBG3, which recruit the DCAF16 E3 ligase. We rank various complexes engaging DCAF16 by their binding free energies and achieve an ordering that is consistent with the trends observed in biophysical assays. Of particular note is our ability to assert the reliance of BRD4 selectivity on a single interfacial glycine residue, which alternative, reduced-sampling MM/GBSA or HADDOCK scoring methodologies fail to achieve. Overall, our protocol shows promise as a generalizable approach to ranking ternary complexes by thermodynamic stability, potentially aiding in the identification of potent new degraders.

title: Accelerating Lead Optimization Away from Anti-Targets: Navigating the Structural Complexity of Promiscuous ADMET Proteins.
authors: Hwang, Howook; Shelley, Mee; Placzek, Andrew; DeMarco, Kevin; Albanese, Steven; Verras, Andreas; Kaila, Neelu; McElwee, Joshua; Campos, Sebastien; Caravella, Justin A; Carreiro, Samantha; Edmondson, Scott D; Kreutter, Kevin D; Kumar, Sheetal; Toms, Angela V; Tummino, Peter J; Whitehead, Lewis; So, Sung-Sau; Inoyama, Daigo; Konze, Kyle; Pelletier, Robert; Xu, Tianchuan; Abel, Robert; Friesner, Richard A; Miller, Edward B
journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
abstract: The development of a small molecule suitable for clinical use involves optimization of ligand binding to an identified target protein but also frequently the reduction of binding to a variety of anti-target proteins known to pose translational risk. These anti-targets, often referred to as ADMET proteins, often contain large, highly flexible binding sites, leading to promiscuous binding of small molecules. This property often frustrates efforts to execute structure-based design against these anti-targets. Here, we demonstrate the application of a combination of induced fit docking and free energy perturbation to structurally enable several of the most common anti-targets: cytochrome P450 isoforms 3A4 and 2D6, the hERG ion channel, and PXR. Crucially, the enforcement of a consensus binding mode across a congeneric series allowed for the efficient exploration of a wide range of receptor conformational space. Results are presented for both public retrospective datasets and prospective application in active drug discovery programs.

title: PlantPAN 5.0: updated database for integrating multiomics evidence and exploring multilayered transcriptional regulatory networks in plants.
authors: Yang, Chien-Wen; Wang, Wen-Lin; Chow, Chi-Nga; Tseng, Kuan-Chieh; Shen, Yen-Lin; Tsao, Ting-Wei; Chien, Yu-Han; Lee, Tzong-Yi; Chang, Wen-Chi
abstract: Plant Promoter Analysis Navigator (PlantPAN) 5.0 (https://plantpan.itps.ncku.edu.tw/) is an integrated multiomics resource for investigating plant cis-regulatory elements and transcriptional regulatory networks. This release expands genome annotations and promoter sequences to 240 species and provides 71 040 transcription factor (TF) annotations and 7762 nonredundant binding matrices. Its companion database, PCBase 3.0, substantially expands ChIP-seq data and newly incorporates ATAC-seq, bisulfite-sequencing, and four Hi-C-based chromatin interaction datasets for Arabidopsis thaliana. The new Differential Analysis function enables comparison of TF binding, chromatin accessibility, and DNA methylation across conditions. The redesigned Promoter Analysis interface provides TF family-level statistics, with a Pattern Overview panel integrating TF-binding site (TFBS) densities, plant DNA large language model-predicted open-chromatin regions, CpG-rich regions, and tandem repeats. Two new modules are introduced: (i) Transcriptome Regulatory Analysis and Coexpression, where candidate regulatory TFs and shared cis-elements in gene sets are prioritized through differential expression and coexpression analysis, and (ii) Interaction Topology Analysis for Chromatin and TFs, where chromatin interaction regions are integrated to reveal potentially coregulated genes and their shared TFs and predicted TFBSs. A Dockerized package enables large-scale local promoter analyses, with data privacy. Therefore, PlantPAN 5.0 is a comprehensive framework for discovering plant transcriptional regulatory mechanisms.

title: Helixpr: a helix-aware periodic representation of DNA sequence for enhancer identification.
authors: Shi, Xiang; Kang, Jiayi; Sun, Nan; Yau, S S-T
abstract: BACKGROUND: Enhancers are distal cis-regulatory elements that play essential roles in gene regulation, development, and disease. Although numerous computational methods have been developed for enhancer identification, commonly used DNA encoding strategies, such as one-hot and k-mer representations, typically treat DNA as a linear symbolic sequence. This simplification ignores the intrinsic geometry of the DNA double helix, where nucleotides are organized along a periodic three-dimensional structure with a helical repeat of approximately 10-11 base pairs.
